clue.text: Bone set? Alarm at fracturing

indicators.note: fracturing breaks the three words apart so their letters can be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor setting a broken bone warns of alarm at the fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like part of the medical picture with 'Bone', but it is fodder: the letters of SET ALARM AT, broken up by 'fracturing', give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the long bones of the foot, between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Ignoring the old, showing a foreign spirit

parts.note: Geist is German for spirit or mind

explanation.surface: Someone shows a foreign attitude by neglecting elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice by age typically means dismissing or overlooking elderly people.

clue.text: Two-stage event, one held in city (half of capital city)

indicators.note: held in puts the numeral for one inside the city's name

parts.note: Bath is an English city in Somerset
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of keeps only the first three letters of the capital's six

explanation.surface: A two-part sporting event takes place in one city, partly in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a spa city in the west of England; the capital city is LONDON, and its first half is LON.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport combines two disciplines, cross-country skiing and rifle shooting.

clue.text: Awake in downpour? Mostly sleeping deeply

indicators.note: in places the word for awake within the shortened downpour
Mostly drops the final letter of the word for a downpour

parts.note: a storm is a heavy downpour of rain
to be up is to be awake and out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone lies awake during a rainstorm, though mostly they sleep soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims STORM to STOR, and 'in' puts UP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near unconsciousness, like being dead to the world.

clue.text: To wander idly round a vehicle is a piece of cake

indicators.note: round means the verb for idling wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to moon about is to wander around idly and dreamily
a car is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone loafing around a car is said to have an easy time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece of cake' suggests 'easy', but here it is literal: a small almond biscuit-cake. MOON wraps round A CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small sweet almond or coconut confection served as a cake or biscuit.

clue.text: Obscene description of right-winger?

definitions.meaning: smutty or indecent jokes and films are called this colour
the colour of the British Conservative Party, so a Tory is described by it

explanation.surface: A rude label for someone on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means smutty, and in Britain it is the Conservatives' party colour, so a Tory is true to it.

clue.text: Composer — man disowned by film director

indicators.note: disowned by means the word man is cast out of the director's surname

parts.note: Ingmar Bergman was a Swedish film director
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer is rejected by a famous filmmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Not likely to be contented with various banalities

indicators.note: various signals that the letters are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tired of assorted clichés is never satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can never be satisfied is never content, however much they get.

clue.text: Inspector that contrived to bend the rules?

indicators.note: contrived means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A police inspector devises a way to bend regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to allow an exception, relaxing a rule slightly.

clue.text: One's put in a fast pace to do for the holder

indicators.note: put in places the contraction inside the word for a gait

parts.note: a canter is a horse's pace between trot and gallop
One's is I'S, the numeral I plus 's

explanation.surface: Someone is placed in a fast pace that will finish off the container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I + S, and 'put in' sets IS inside CANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a container, a vessel for holding tea, film or gas.

clue.text: Tree needing the northern earth?

parts.note: the plane is a tree, common in London streets
in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t' (as in 'on t' moor')

explanation.surface: A tree needs northern soil to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' looks like soil for the tree, but with a question mark it defines our world, one of many. The northern English dialect form t' for 'the' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth is one example of a world orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: Group of companies having concern linked to pound -about time

indicators.note: about means the pieces wrap around the abbreviation for time

parts.note: care is concern or worry
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A business group is worried about the pound and short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: CARE and L run together, and 'about' puts them round T: CAR-T-EL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an association of firms that fix prices and limit competition.

clue.text: One slow to move to relaunched Tories

indicators.note: relaunched suggests something rebuilt anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sluggish politician defects to the newly relaunched Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'to' is set in front as written; 'relaunched' rearranges TORIES into RTOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile is proverbially slow, as in the fable with the hare.

clue.text: Defamation about the shifty Scotsman?

indicators.note: about means the word for defamation goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: slander is spoken defamation

indicators.note: shifty suggests letters that move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Libellous talk surrounds a shifty Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifty' turns THE into HET, and 'about' puts SLANDER round it: S-HET-LANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An islander from the far north of Scotland is a Scot, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Fail to decide which garden to occupy?

definitions.text: Fail to decide which garden to occupy?

parts.words: Fail to decide which garden to occupy?
parts.note: someone undecided between two neighbouring gardens literally perches on the boundary between them

explanation.surface: Someone cannot choose between neighbouring gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay neutral, refusing to take either side in a dispute.

clue.text: Choreography for the RUC Water Music?

parts.note: a tap supplies water
a dance is a piece of music written for dancing

explanation.surface: Dance steps arranged for Handel's Water Music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water Music' looks like Handel's suite, but the words split: TAP (water source) and DANCE (a tune to dance to).
explanation.definitionFit: It is a style of dancing with metal-tipped shoes, so a routine of it is choreography.

clue.text: Remain involved in favouring introduction of "honest young tree planting?

indicators.note: involved in places the word for remain inside the word for favouring

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
to rest is to remain

indicators.note: introduction of takes only the first letter

explanation.surface: Staying engaged in support of letting young people plant trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts REST inside FOR, giving FORESTR, then 'introduction of young' adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the science and work of planting and managing woodland.

clue.text: Caught some friend backing nonsense

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: backing means the following pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: part means some of something
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend is caught supporting rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns PART + PAL into LAPTRAP, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: It is pretentious empty talk, rubbish meant to win applause.

clue.text: Lot of water found in endangered seam

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mass of water is discovered flooding a threatened coal seam.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sea between Africa and Arabia, a large body of water.

clue.text: English novelist not first in crowd

indicators.note: not first drops the opening letter of the novelist's surname

parts.note: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist

explanation.surface: An English writer is not the leading figure in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly mob of people.

clue.text: Dance close, mostly — sexy? Not half

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word meaning close

parts.note: to bolt a door is to close it

indicators.note: Not half keeps only half of the word, its first three letters

parts.note: erotic means sexy

explanation.surface: A dance gets close and steamy, but only up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slang for 'very much', but it cuts EROTIC to ERO; BOLT mostly is BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Spanish dance in triple time, and Ravel's famous orchestral piece.

clue.text: Pig depicted in advert on bus?

indicators.note: depicted in puts the animal inside the short word for an advert

parts.note: an ad is an advert
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A pig appears in an advertisement on the side of a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on bus' looks like where the advert is, but it is the definition: a passenger is on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a bus, ship or plane is being on board as a passenger.

clue.text: Sack founder of RUC chemists?

definitions.meaning: to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job
Jesse ... founded the ... chain of British chemist shops

explanation.surface: Dismiss the man who started a chain of pharmacies.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the push is to fire them; Jesse Boot founded the British chemists' chain named after him.

clue.text: Hard up, though not very short?

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for very is removed

parts.note: hard up means short of money, unable to pay debts

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash, yet not too badly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like part of 'hard up', but it is the definition: curt or rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short with someone is being curt, rudely brusque.

clue.text: Children found among various electors in Essex town

indicators.note: found among puts the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
various signals that the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Children are among assorted voters in an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: COLESTER (the anagram of ELECTORS, from 'various') takes CH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a historic town in the English county of Essex, claimed as Britain's oldest.

clue.text: Like retsina, having no initial aroma

indicators.note: having no initial drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: Retsina is described as having no initial bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A reek is a strong unpleasant smell.
